speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for your patience. To better understand your condition, could you please describe when the vaginal bleeding started and what color or consistency it is? Additionally, how would you rate your abdominal pain on a scale from 1 to 10?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 38 weeks' gestation. The patient reports experiencing vaginal bleeding for the past hour accompanied by severe abdominal pain. She mentions that she felt contractions before the onset of the bleeding, but the contractions ceased once the bleeding began. Her first childbirth was a cesarean section due to nonreassuring fetal heart rate.

speaker: Doctor
text: That history of a prior cesarean section combined with severe pain and bleeding is highly concerning for uterine rupture. Have you experienced any loss of fetal movement, dizziness, or pain specifically in the lower abdomen or shoulder? REQUEST TEST: Fetal Heart Rate Monitoring; REQUEST TEST: Maternal Vitals and CBC.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pulse: 110/min, Blood Pressure: 90/60 mm Hg, Respiratory Rate: 17/min; Fetal Heart Rate Monitoring: Shows recurrent variable decelerations; Hemoglobin: 10.2 g/dL (decreased); Platelets: 200,000 /μL.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Vaginal bleeding. I also have Severe abdominal pain, History of contractions that stopped, Previous cesarean delivery.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: One previous childbirth via cesarean section. No other significant past medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, occasional alcohol consumption. Works as an elementary school teacher.

speaker: Patient
text: Reports feeling the baby move before the onset of symptoms but is unsure about movement since the symptoms started. Denies any recent trauma to the abdomen or any urinary symptoms. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.
